_comment: Row 249. Run from a detached standalone scratch copy with toolchain/bin/bd-mutate. M1 restores the exact forking ps census: the named catcher must fail at the zero-launch tripwire. M2 restores the invalid cross-time verdict: the fixture deterministically reaps a group member after proving it was in the snapshot, so the named catcher must fail on that exact pid. The separate row249_group_census_transform_control.json applies M1 while running only an import control and must ESCAPE, proving M1 is caught by the behavioral assertions rather than by parsing, collection, or import failure.
subject: row 249 -- a valid process-group snapshot survives a peer exit without admitting a self-counted census fork

mutants.label: M1 the census forks ps into the caller's group and counts its own instrument again
mutants.new:
result = subprocess.run(["ps", "-eo", "pgid=,pid=,stat="],
                            capture_output=True, text=True)
    rows = [line.split() for line in result.stdout.splitlines()
            if line.split()]
    return [row[1] for row in rows
            if row[0] == str(pgid) and not row[2].startswith("Z")]

mutants.label: M2 a snapshot is rejected when its proven-live member exits before a later stat
mutants.old:
assert str(probe.pid) in reported, (
            "the valid snapshot lost the exact member that was live when read")
mutants.new:
vanished = [pid for pid in reported
                    if _w1_stat_pgid_and_state(pid) is None]
        assert not vanished, (
            "the census reported pids that no longer exist: %r" % vanished)
